jobs.title: Global Public Policy Manager, Compute, Infrastructure & Sovereign AI

reading.body:
Two open AI policy and governance roles are visible in this dataset, one in Munich and one remote in the United States.

The sample is too small to describe a market. Two postings, one from a consultancy and one from a model developer, cannot establish a trend in hiring volume, pay, or geography. What they do show is the shape of the work: one role sits with a European advisory firm, the other with an AI company and is explicitly about compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI. That second title is the more informative of the two, because it names the physical substrate directly. Policy work at an AI lab is now partly about where machines sit and how they are powered, not only about model behavior or regulation in the abstract.

The listing sources include USAJobs, several aggregators, remote boards, and company career pages, so the pipeline reaches federal, European, and direct-from-employer postings. That breadth makes the count of two more likely a thin category than a thin search. Governance and policy is a small slice of AI hiring relative to engineering, and this data cannot say how small, because it carries no comparison category and no historical baseline.

Nothing here supports a claim about growth, salaries, or which countries are competing hardest. It is a snapshot of two openings on one day, and it should be read as an illustration of what the roles look like rather than as evidence about how many exist.
